reviews.title: be quiet, Tell Everyone
reviews.comment: If you are using an air cooling system for your computer, then you should be using  "be quiet" fans to cool it. The name says it all, so let me explain. I could not get it to compute in my mind to use water to cool my cpu and/or video card. Let me think about this my MB = $199, My CPU = $750, My Video Card = 1000 and now you want me to add water (water cooling system approximately $299.) to this equation. This makes no sense to me, but I was using a very loud 100% copper cooler. I decided to make some changes and ordered a be quiet Pure Rock Pro 3 cooler. As soon as I installed it and turned my computer on I was totally shocked. NO CPU FAN NOISE. NONE. ZILCH. ZERO. I could not believe my ears. Then  I began running all kinds of cpu, memory, video card, motherboard, and power supply test just to see if the cpu would heat up causing the fans to spin up. It did and the fans increased in speed but still NO SOUND came from the cooler itself. I could only get the cooler to make noise I could hear by running my 16 core cpu at 100%. Now running al cores and threads at 100% caused my temps to rise up to approximately 87C. Not good for long periods of time but doable. Over time and my trust in the "be quiet" line of products I switched over to the be quiet! Dark Rock Elite - TDP 280W CPU Cooler. Their line of air coolers are top notch. They are quiet and help to keep your cpu cool under all circumstances. I have run my computer in a lab setting testing medical simulations that run my computer processor at all cores running 100%, 16 cores/32 threads running 100% on the processor for months. The system never crashed unless I rebooted it and it was cooled only using air. The "be quiet" line of cpu coolers work great. I am very happy to have experienced this companies product as it works for me.
reviews.author: RGiorgio

reviews.title: What a beast of a fan cooler
reviews.comment: The moment you open it, out of the box, it's BIG, HEAVY, and you can tell it's made out of quality stuff.  LOVE the long screw driver that it came with.  In fact, I used the damn screw driver for everything to build my entire computer - thank you for including that!  Installation was a breeze (just be careful not to apply too much pressure to the CPU like I did like a newbie, had to figure out why the PC would boot, oops).  Connects easily to the motherboard.  Thing runs DEAD SILENT even on performance mode.  When I play games, I hear my GPU fans revving up but never this CPU cooler.  I went for the silent - no RGB - classy setup with Fractal North mid tower case, silent wing case fans x3.  I love my setup and the way it turned out!  I'll always buy be quiet products from now on.
reviews.author: JK

reviews.title: i5-14600K -- No Issues
reviews.comment: Paired with an i5-14600K CPU.  This PCU tends to run at a higher temp than a chip like the i5-13600 or Ryzen 7 7700X.  With that said, this cooler has prevented any 'red flag' temps, even under heavy load.  The fans move a tremendous amount of air, and the noise is - acceptable - when at high fan speeds.  Fitment COULD be an issue, as the cooler is tall.  Be sure to verify proper clearances off the MB to your case cover.
reviews.author: Water_Spider_Detailing

reviews.title: Almost perfect, but...
reviews.comment: This would've easily been 5-stars because the cooler works great! BUT, the instructions were a bit vague and there is BARELY enough lead wire on the fan cables to install it without much more work. This should have been a very straight-forward installation by simply installing the bracket and mounting the fan. I had to remove the video card as well so I could reach the lead wires under the cooler to connect the fans together after attaching them. I don't think an additional 2-3 inches would've increased costs that much. The cooler itself works very well and one of the fans is adjustable to be able to fit over the RAM modules. Again, this idea wasn't really thought out because if I had all four DIMM slots populated, the cooler would fit but I wouldn't be able to put the glass panel back on the case. All-in-all it's a decent air cooler, but needs some refinement on the design and cable lengths. It is extremely quiet even when you have it running at full speed. A great value for the money, but make sure there's plenty of room!
reviews.author: JBKB

reviews.title: Super reliable and quiet!
reviews.comment: I want to start by saying I’ve tried just about everything—including full custom water cooling setups across multiple systems. This time around, I was looking for something more reliable, low-maintenance, and most importantly, quiet. One thing many people overlook with AIOs and water coolers is the noise. Between the fans and the pump, they can often get louder than expected. But with this cooler, it’s almost silent. It also features a switch between Quiet and Performance mode—I leave mine on the standard setting, and it handles everything flawlessly. I’m running a 7950X, which is known to run hot, and this cooler keeps it in the 50s under load. Even during intense gaming sessions, I’ve had no issues with overheating. The design is another highlight. The fan looks sleek and modern—especially in my blackout build with no RGB. The subtle LED ring on the cooler adds just the right touch of elegance without going overboard. Overall, it’s a super reliable cooler that I’d highly recommend to anyone looking for a no-fuss, efficient solution. It’s especially great if you’re on the AMD platform and want something that will handle future upgrades with ease.
